17706273.summary: Faron announced first overall survival data from its BEXMAB phase 1/2 trial at median 14.9-month follow-up. In 21 treatment-naïve HR-MDS patients, median OS was not reached for TP53 wildtype and monoallelic mutated patients. Biallelic TP53 mutated patients (67% of TP53-mutated cohort) achieved median OS of 8.8 months, in line with historical data. Data supports progression toward BEXERA, a planned randomized study of bexmarilimab plus azacitidine in frontline HR-MDS.
17706273.brief: Faron reports encouraging OS data from BEXMAB trial of bexmarilimab in higher-risk MDS patients, with median OS not yet reached in key subgroups.
17706273.take: Early survival data showing non-inferiority in aggressive biallelic cohort and ongoing survival in other groups supports clinical development; detailed dataset awaited at scientific meeting later in 2026.

17706233.summary: Neuberger Private Equity Partners Limited repurchased 30,000 Class A Shares on 24 July 2026 via Jefferies International at prices between £14.46 and £14.64 per share. All purchased shares will be cancelled. Following cancellation, outstanding Class A Shares total 40,429,301, with an additional 3,150,408 held in treasury. The buyback was conducted under shareholder authority granted on 11 June 2026.
17706233.brief: NBPE completes 30,000 Class A share buyback at £14.46-£14.64, reducing outstanding shares to 40.4m.
17706233.take: Routine capital management action; share cancellation reduces share count, potentially supporting per-share metrics, though immaterial scale suggests this is incremental shareholder return activity rather than transformational.

17706232.summary: Between 20–24 July 2026, OSB Group repurchased 14,243 ordinary shares at volume-weighted average prices ranging from 553.64p to 560.95p across London Stock Exchange and alternative venues via Jefferies. Shares purchased across LSE, CBOE BXE, CBOE CXE, and Aquis Exchange. Following cancellation, issued share count falls to 341,550,929; no treasury shares held. Programme commenced 5 March 2026.
17706232.brief: OSB Group completed buyback of 14,243 shares at average 556p; shares to be cancelled.
17706232.take: Routine execution of disclosed buyback programme; capital returns via share cancellation reduce share count but signal no immediate growth catalyst or cash deployment concern.

17706164.summary: Pershing Square Holdings purchased 33,333 public shares on 24 July 2026 at an average price of $49.76 USD through Jefferies. The breakdown shows 22,765 shares traded on LSE (PSH ticker) averaging 3,729 pence ($49.75) and 10,568 shares on the dollar listing (PSHD) averaging $49.77. The NAV per share was $76.01 as of 21 July. Post-buyback, PSH has 173.6m shares outstanding with 37.3m shares held in treasury.
17706164.brief: PSH repurchases 33,333 shares at average $49.76; holds 37.3m treasury shares.
17706164.take: Routine share buyback below NAV signals capital management but modest scale; non-event for most retail investors tracking the fund's NAV accretion and treasury building strategy.

17706381.summary: Sonesitatug vedotin (Sone-Ve) demonstrated statistically significant overall survival improvement in 2nd+ line CLDN18.2-positive advanced gastric/GEJ cancers versus investigator's choice therapy in the Phase III CLARITY-Gastric01 trial. The drug met dual primary endpoints of OS in 3rd+ line and achieved key secondary endpoint of OS in overall 2nd+ line population. Results enable expansion of CLDN18.2 positivity threshold to ≥25% expression, covering ~60% of patients (~183,500 annually across US, EU, China, Japan). This is AstraZeneca's first pivotal readout from its wholly-owned ADC portfolio.
17706381.brief: AstraZeneca's Sone-Ve shows survival benefit in advanced gastric cancers, first anti-CLDN18.2 ADC to achieve this.
17706381.take: Positive catalyst for AstraZeneca's oncology pipeline with first-in-class potential in large gastric cancer market; strong survival data likely supports regulatory approval pathway and commercial prospects.

17706380.summary: Trustpilot Group PLC purchased 378,500 ordinary shares on LSE during 20-24 July 2026 via Deutsche Bank at prices ranging from 243.80p to 272.00p, with a volume-weighted average of 250.07-267.79p daily. Since the buyback programme commenced 25 March 2026, the company has repurchased 3,858,256 shares for cancellation at approximately £9.6m (excluding costs). All shares are being cancelled, reducing issued capital.
17706380.brief: Trustpilot bought back 378,500 shares (20-24 July) at 243.8-272p; 3.86m shares cancelled since March for £9.6m.
17706380.take: Ongoing capital return supports EPS accretion and signals management confidence; routine execution of announced programme with no new material announcements signals steady, predictable capital allocation.

17706382.summary: Tortilla Mexican Grill PLC has published its Annual Report and Accounts for the 52 weeks ended 28 December 2025, alongside the Notice of its 2026 Annual General Meeting. The AGM will be held on 25 August 2026 at 11:00am at CMS Cameron McKenna Nabarro Olswang LLP offices in London. Documents are available on the company website, with printed copies posted to shareholders who requested hard copy. The company operates Europe's largest fast-casual Mexican restaurant brand with over 1,200 employees.
17706382.brief: Tortilla publishes 2025 annual report and AGM notice; meeting scheduled for 25 August 2026.
17706382.take: Routine disclosure of annual results documentation and AGM arrangements; no material news beyond procedural notification of shareholder meeting and full-year accounts publication.

17706359.summary: Vietnam Holding Limited's June 2026 investor report highlights a disconnect between Vietnam's robust economic data—8.2% Q2 GDP growth, 21% export rises, record $34.7bn FDI—and depressed equity valuations. The fund's NAV declined 0.3% in June. Portfolio trades at 10x forward earnings despite ~20% expected earnings growth; top 10 holdings at 8.5x. World Bank reclassified Vietnam as Upper-Middle Income; IMF raised 2026 growth forecast to 7.5%; FTSE Russell promotion to Secondary Emerging Market status imminent in September.
17706359.brief: VNH June 2026 monthly report shows NAV down 0.3% amid Vietnam's strong economic fundamentals but subdued equity valuations.
17706359.take: Mixed signal: strong macro backdrop suggests value opportunity, but persistent foreign selling and weak market sentiment indicate investors remain cautious on Vietnam despite fundamentals. Long-term positioning trumps near-term price momentum.

17706229.summary: Fund Manager Paul Niven will conduct a live presentation for F&C Investment Trust plc on Tuesday 4 August 2026 at 11:00 a.m. BST via the Investor Meet Company platform. The session is open to existing and potential shareholders, with pre-submission of questions available until 9:00 a.m. on 3 August. Investors can register free on the platform at investormeetcompany.com.
17706229.brief: F&C Investment Trust to hold investor presentation on 4 August via Investor Meet Company platform.
17706229.take: Routine investor engagement activity; presentation opportunity allows direct dialogue with fund manager but carries no material news or strategic implications.

17706230.summary: CRISM Therapeutics (AIM: CRTX), a clinical-stage drug delivery company developing ChemoSeed for localised chemotherapy, disclosed its major shareholder composition following independent third-party analysis. Miton UK Smaller Companies Fund leads with 9.47% (7.5m shares), followed by Executive Chairman Andrew Webb at 9.22% (7.3m shares), CSO Dr Christopher McConville at 6.30% (5.0m shares), and Brian Murray at 6.20% (4.9m shares). Five other shareholders hold between 3.02% and 5.07% each. No single shareholder controls the company.
17706230.brief: CRISM Therapeutics publishes shareholder register analysis identifying eight significant shareholders holding 3%+ stakes as of 30 June 2026.
17706230.take: Routine regulatory disclosure of shareholder register findings; shows balanced ownership structure with no dominant stakeholder. Market impact likely neutral as this is standard governance transparency.

17706231.summary: On 24 July 2026, JTC Employer Solutions Trustee Limited, acting as trustee of Ultimate Products' Employee Benefit Trust, purchased 28,030 ordinary shares at 56.8 pence per share. Following this transaction, the EBT holds 3,601,511 ordinary shares, representing approximately 4.2% of the company's issued share capital. The EBT holds shares for employee benefit and to satisfy vesting under the company's share incentive schemes.
17706231.brief: Ultimate Products' EBT purchases 28,030 shares at 56.8p, bringing trust holding to 4.2% of issued capital.
17706231.take: Routine share purchase by employee benefit trust to support ongoing incentive schemes; typical corporate governance activity with no material market implications for investors.

17706234.summary: Warpaint London PLC (AIM: W7L) has commenced a share buyback programme with maximum consideration of £2.5 million, ending 31 December 2026. Shares will be held in treasury to satisfy future employee share scheme obligations, reducing shareholder dilution. The programme uses part of the company's £20.6 million cash balance as of 30 June 2026. Shore Capital Stockbrokers will execute purchases on an irrevocable, non-discretionary basis within regulatory parameters, though daily volumes may exceed safe harbour thresholds.
17706234.brief: Warpaint London launches £2.5m share buyback programme to run until end-2026, with shares held in treasury.
17706234.take: Share buybacks signal management confidence in valuation and efficient capital allocation, returning value while maintaining liquidity; generally viewed as positive by markets unless execution concerns arise.

17706235.summary: On 24 July 2026, Sosandar PLC purchased 500,000 ordinary shares at 11.965p per share under shareholder authority granted in April 2026, representing 0.2% of issued capital. Shares will be held in treasury. The company's total voting rights stand at 217,151,611 ordinary shares after accounting for 31,074,902 shares held in treasury against total issued capital of 248,403,651 shares.
17706235.brief: Sosandar repurchases 500,000 shares at 11.965p as part of authorized buyback program.
17706235.take: Share buyback at modest scale suggests capital management confidence; likely market non-event absent broader earnings context or strategic signaling.

17706236.summary: Scancell Holdings (AIM: SCLP), an immuno-oncology company, completed a significantly oversubscribed retail offer raising £2.7m gross (approximately $3.6m) at 9 pence per share, issuing 30,004,836 new shares. Combined with the institutional placing of 144,444,444 shares, the total fundraise reached £15.7m (c.$21.0m). The offer was expanded from an initial £2.3m target due to strong investor demand, with allocations scaled back and preference given to existing shareholders. Admission to AIM is expected 28 July 2026, bringing total issued share capital to 1,212,230,683 ordinary shares.
17706236.brief: Scancell's oversubscribed retail offer raises £2.7m at 9p per share; total fundraise reaches £15.7m including institutional placing.
17706236.take: Strong oversubscription signals investor confidence in the late-stage clinical immunotherapy programme and fundraising execution; positive validation though dilution to existing shareholders is material at ~144m shares.

17706237.summary: Technology Minerals PLC has extended the St Patrick Research Permit (PI No. 30,858) in northwest Spain for two years, now valid until 21 June 2028. The licence includes the historic Aramo Mine, held through Spanish subsidiary Asturmet Recursos S.L. Previous work identified high-grade mineralisation with assays up to 28% copper, 1.88% cobalt and 0.1-1.68% nickel. The extension supports the Mantle strategy to strengthen UK supply security for designated critical minerals and does not commit the company to material further expenditure.
17706237.brief: Technology Minerals secures two-year extension of St Patrick copper-cobalt-nickel research permit in Spain until June 2028.
17706237.take: Non-event with modest positive undertone. Extension secures valuable optionality for critical minerals exposure aligned with UK policy, but lacks immediate development trigger or capital commitment, limiting near-term catalysts.

17706238.summary: JM published circular detailing £1bn shareholder returns following July 2026 Honeywell sale of Catalyst Technologies. Special dividend of 476.5 pence per share (£800m) payable 28 August to shareholders of record 14 August, with equivalent USD payments to ADR holders from 8 September. Accompanied by 3-for-4 share consolidation effective 17 August to maintain share price stability. General Meeting scheduled 11 August 2026 for shareholder approval. Additional routine authorities sought for share allotment and buyback programmes through 2027 AGM.
17706238.brief: Johnson Matthey returns £1bn to shareholders via £800m special dividend and £200m buyback following Catalyst Technologies sale.
17706238.take: Positive signal: substantial capital return demonstrates confidence post-divestiture and commitment to shareholder value, though consolidation is purely technical with no immediate economic benefit.

17706239.summary: 80 Mile PLC placed 283.6 million ordinary shares at 0.67p per share (10% discount to 24 July close of 0.75p), raising approximately £1.9m before expenses. Proceeds fund general expenses, Ferrandina biofuels plant restart in Italy, Finland project preparation for sale, and Dundas sampling. Shares represent ~5% dilution; admission to AIM expected 30 July 2026. Company has US$100m committed funded expenditure across two joint venture drilling campaigns in Greenland (Jameson and Disko-Nuussuaq) launching H2 2026.
17706239.brief: 80 Mile raises £1.9m via placing of 283.6m shares at 0.67p to fund exploration and plant restart.
17706239.take: Capital raise supports near-term operational momentum with major joint venture drilling campaigns funded externally, though 5% dilution and discount signal financing pressure; market likely positive on project momentum but cautious on valuation.

17706240.summary: HyProMag USA (50:50 owned by CoTec and Mkango) is fast-tracking commissioning of finished NdFeB magnet production equipment in Dallas-Fort Worth for H1 2027, utilizing up to 20 tonnes of magnet blocks from UK/German HyProMag operations. Full integrated Texas Hub with Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (HPMS) technology targets Q2 2028 start-up with initial capacity of ~400 metric tonnes recycled magnets and ~278 metric tonnes co-products (678 total), ramping to 1,526 metric tonnes. Strategy enables early customer engagement, product qualification, and de-risks market entry ahead of full domestic recycling operations.
17706240.brief: HyProMag USA accelerates magnet finishing capability in Texas, targeting H1 2027 production ahead of full integrated operations in Q2 2028.
17706240.take: De-risking strategy through phased commissioning and early revenue generation likely viewed positively; demonstrates pragmatic execution, though forward-looking statements carry inherent execution risk and equipment procurement uncertainties.

17706241.summary: Edinburgh Worldwide Investment Trust plc has appointed Singer Capital Markets as its sole corporate broker and financial adviser, effective immediately. Deutsche Numis, the outgoing broker, provided support during the initial phase following the Board's appointment in April 2026, facilitating an orderly transition. Singer Capital Markets' corporate finance contact is James Maxwell, with sales handled by Alan Geeves and Sam Greatrex.
17706241.brief: Edinburgh Worldwide Investment Trust appoints Singer Capital Markets as sole corporate broker, replacing Deutsche Numis.
17706241.take: Routine broker appointment change; market unlikely to react materially. Indicates normal operational continuity post-Board transition in April 2026.

17706228.summary: Everyman Media Group achieved 2.6m admissions (up 20.5%) and £70.0m revenue (up 23.9%) in H1 2026, with adjusted EBITDA rising 32% to £10.8m. Average ticket price increased 4.1% to £12.97 and market share expanded 60 basis points to 6.4%. Net debt fell 29% to £17.1m. Directors expect full-year 2026 performance marginally ahead of 2025, though cautious due to economic conditions and planned H2 IT infrastructure investment. Board continues assessing delisting, with further announcement expected by end-August 2026.
17706228.brief: Everyman Media reports H1 2026 admissions up 20.5%, revenue up 23.9% to £70.0m. Net debt down 29% to £17.1m.
17706228.take: Strong operational momentum with significant revenue and margin growth suggests market execution strength, but director caution on FY outlook, upcoming delisting discussions, and material H2 investment spending may temper enthusiasm.

17706227.summary: Costain Group PLC's CEO Alex Vaughan and CFO Helen Willis will conduct an investor Q&A session on 17 August 2026 at 10:00am via Investor Meet Company platform, open to existing and potential shareholders. Questions can be submitted pre-event until 10:00am on 16 August or during the live presentation. The H1 2026 results will be published on 13 August 2026. Registration is free via investormeetcompany.com.
17706227.brief: Costain to host investor Q&A on 17 August via Investor Meet Company following H1 2026 results release on 13 August.
17706227.take: Routine disclosure; routine investor engagement activity ahead of half-year results. No material news or read-through to market sentiment.

17706226.summary: NCB Tier 1 Sukuk Limited has cancelled the admission to trading of its USD 1,250,000,000 Additional Tier 1 Capital Certificates (ISIN: XS2280537916) on the London Stock Exchange's ISM platform, effective immediately as of 27 July 2026. The announcement provides no explanation for the delisting decision.
17706226.brief: NCB Tier 1 Sukuk Limited cancels listing of USD 1.25bn Additional Tier 1 Capital Certificates on LSE.
17706226.take: Delisting of a large Tier 1 sukuk suggests potential refinancing, maturity, or issuer strategic decision; lack of detail limits market interpretation but typically non-disruptive for institutional holders.

17706224.summary: Geoffrey Wilding, Executive Chairman of Victoria PLC (LSE: VCP), purchased 150,000 Ordinary Shares of 5p each on 24 July 2026 at 67.42p per share on the London Stock Exchange. Following this transaction, Wilding's beneficial interest increased to 22,588,650 shares, representing 19.58% of issued share capital. Victoria is an international flooring manufacturer and distributor headquartered in Worcester, with operations across nine countries and approximately 5,000-6,300 employees.
17706224.brief: Victoria PLC Executive Chairman Geoffrey Wilding purchases 150,000 shares, increasing stake to 19.58%.
17706224.take: Management share purchase at 67.42p signals insider confidence in valuation and company prospects, typically viewed positively by markets as alignment with shareholder interests.

17706225.summary: Mark H Dixon and Diana Dixon, acting through Rock Nominees Limited, crossed a major holdings threshold in SkinBioTherapeutics PLC on 23 July 2026. Their voting rights increased from 28.359% (73.5m shares) to 29.324% (76m shares), triggering notification to the FCA on 24 July 2026. The holding comprises ordinary shares only with no financial instruments involved.
17706225.brief: Mark and Diana Dixon's holding in SkinBioTherapeutics increased to 29.32% of voting rights via Rock Nominees Limited.
17706225.take: Routine disclosure of incremental shareholding increase by existing major shareholders; no strategic implications evident, typical threshold notification with marginal stake accumulation.

17706245.summary: Sealand Capital Galaxy (LSE: SCGL) announced establishment of SaturnGlitter, a new AI data security platform operating through newly incorporated Hong Kong subsidiary SaturnGlitter (HK) Limited. A specialist technology team contributes proprietary technology and expertise while Sealand provides commercial platform and corporate governance. The platform addresses growing demand for secure AI deployment across financial services, healthcare, industrial sectors, digital identity and public sector infrastructure, complementing Sealand's broader AI ecosystem strategy spanning computing infrastructure, enterprise software and digital finance.
17706245.brief: Sealand launches SaturnGlitter, an AI data security platform via Hong Kong subsidiary, targeting financial services, healthcare and public sector.
17706245.take: Strategic expansion into adjacent AI infrastructure addressing real market need for secure data governance; demonstrates execution on AI strategy but lacks specific revenue projections or partnership details to validate near-term commercial traction.

17706243.summary: Tristel PLC has commercially launched 3T Pro, a premium subscription tier within its 3T digital compliance platform. The launch formalizes a three-tier structure: free entry-level training/compliance tools, mid-tier with device traceability, and 3T Pro offering advanced customization, workflows, audit reporting and data architecture. Existing traceability users receive transitional licensing protection. Built by Tristel's in-house software team, 3T Pro addresses growing healthcare compliance demands and represents the company's first paid digital offering, establishing a recurring revenue stream alongside its core chlorine dioxide-based infection prevention products.
17706243.brief: Tristel launches 3T Pro, a paid premium tier for its digital compliance platform, diversifying revenue beyond core disinfection products.
17706243.take: Positive signal: diversifies revenue streams beyond cyclical disinfectant sales into scalable SaaS recurring revenue, though magnitude unclear and uptake unproven. Appeals to investors seeking growth into higher-margin digital services.

17706242.summary: Aston Martin provided additional details on its new Senior Secured Notes due 2029 financing announced July 22, 2026. The Notes remain secured by a pledge over shares in Aston Martin Lagonda Limited (indirect parent entity), while new financing is secured against assets in a newly incorporated subsidiary. A separate new Group subsidiary has been designated as an "unrestricted subsidiary" under the Notes' indenture, allowing greater financial flexibility.
17706242.brief: Aston Martin clarifies debt financing structure following investor questions on July 22 announcement.
17706242.take: Clarification announcement suggests investor concern over financing structure; the designation of unrestricted subsidiaries may indicate debt restructuring to preserve operational flexibility, though lack of material terms limits market impact.

17706246.summary: Beowulf Mining released a CEO interview covering a recently completed capital raise and progress at its Kallak Iron Ore Project in Sweden and Graphite Anode Materials Plant in Finland. The company is a Nordic-focused exploration and development business operating in Sweden and Finland across multiple commodities. No specific financial figures, investment amounts, or project milestones were detailed in the announcement itself.
17706246.brief: CEO Ed Bowie discusses recent strategic investment and updates on Kallak iron ore and Finland graphite projects.
17706246.take: Primarily a media relations exercise providing no new material information; investors should review the full interview video for substantive project or funding details to assess impact.

17706109.summary: Chet Patel, a PDMR/director at MITIE Group PLC, acquired 18,838 ordinary shares at 141.96 pence per share on 5 June 2025, totalling £26,742.42. Suman Patel, a person closely associated with Chet Patel, purchased 40,345 ordinary shares at 98.6173 pence per share on 3 October 2023, worth £39,787.15. Combined, the transactions represent 59,183 shares acquired across the two transactions.
17706109.brief: MITIE director Chet Patel and closely associated person purchased shares totalling 59,183 ordinary shares.
17706109.take: Director share purchases signal insider confidence in the business, typically viewed positively; however, dated transactions (2023-2025) mean limited immediate market read. Routine regulatory disclosure with modest positive sentiment undertones.

17706108.summary: Matthew Ciardiello, 44, joins Helix's board as CFO effective 31 July 2026, replacing Ryan Neates. Ciardiello brings 20+ years' natural resources experience, including previous CFO roles at NASDAQ-listed Magellan Petroleum and helium exploration expertise from Poplar Resources. The move consolidates finance functions in the US where Helix operates. Neates will assist with UK financial and reporting matters. A Poplar Resources subsidiary filed Chapter 7 bankruptcy in May 2025 while Ciardiello was a director, proceedings ongoing.
17706108.brief: Helix Exploration appoints US-based Matthew Ciardiello as CFO, replacing UK-based Ryan Neates from 31 July 2026.
17706108.take: Operationally sound appointment aligning finance leadership with US operations; however, Ciardiello's prior directorship connection to a bankrupt entity warrants investor scrutiny on governance oversight and due diligence processes.

17706099.summary: JPMorgan Asset Management Holdings Inc., via UK subsidiary JPMorgan Asset Management (UK) Limited, crossed a major shareholding threshold in Plus500 Ltd on 23 July 2026. The entity now holds 6.102801% of voting rights (4.2m shares), comprising 5.249061% direct voting rights and 0.853740% through cash-settled equity swaps. This represents an increase from the previous 5.611502% position, notified to the issuer on 24 July 2026.
17706099.brief: JPMorgan Asset Management increases Plus500 stake to 6.1% through holding structure notification.
17706099.take: Routine disclosure of increased institutional ownership; JPMorgan's build demonstrates confidence but no material implications for retail investors absent further strategic developments.

17706097.summary: Lorenz Werndle, 51, appointed independent non-executive director effective immediately, replacing Donald McAlister who steps down 4 August 2026 due to other commitments. Werndle is CFO of LSE-listed Kavango Resources plc with extensive mining, M&A and African experience, including prior CFO roles at Nasdaq-listed Blue Gold and positions at Mwana Africa, Lonrho and Ambrian. He becomes Audit and Risk Committee Chairman and joins Nomination and Remuneration Committees. Holds no company shares or options.
17706097.brief: Tertiary Minerals appoints Lorenz Werndle as independent NED, replacing Donald McAlister after 25 years.
17706097.take: Experienced sector replacement with relevant African mining credentials likely viewed positively; succession of long-serving director with continuity of skills suggests board stability and supports company's Zambian exploration focus.

17706095.summary: EJF Investments Ltd has declared a quarterly dividend of 2.8625 pence per share for the quarter ended 30 June 2026. The ex-dividend date is 6 August 2026, with payment on or about 28 August 2026 to shareholders on the register at 7 August 2026. Shareholders may elect to receive dividends in USD via Computershare by 10 August 2026. The company targets 8.8p annual dividend yield and invests primarily in US financial institution loans and CDO equity tranches.
17706095.brief: EJF Investments declares Q2 2026 dividend of 2.8625p per share, payable 28 August.
17706095.take: Routine quarterly dividend maintains consistent income distribution for shareholders; no material news beyond expected periodic capital return in line with stated dividend policy.

17706066.summary: Jet2 plc purchased 412,152 ordinary shares between 20-24 July 2026 via Jefferies International at volume-weighted average prices ranging from 14.35p to 14.65p per share, completing the first tranche of its buyback programme announced 8 July 2026. Following cancellation, issued shares reduce to 190,106,364. Shares purchased across AIM, TRQX, BATE, AQXE, and CHIX venues at prices broadly in the 14.40p-14.50p range.
17706066.brief: Jet2 completes first tranche of share buyback, purchasing 412,152 shares at average 14.50p for cancellation.
17706066.take: Routine capital management execution within shareholder-approved authority. Share count reduction modestly accretive to earnings per share but signals no urgent capital needs; implies management confidence in valuation and disciplined capital deployment.

17706063.summary: Angling Direct PLC purchased 60,000 ordinary shares at 48 pence per share on 24 July 2026 via Singer Capital Markets, to be held in treasury. The purchase was executed as a single transaction at 14:03:28 on AIMX. The company's total issued share capital remains 77,267,304 shares, with 4,983,000 held in treasury, leaving 72,284,304 shares carrying voting rights. This forms part of an extended buyback programme announced on 10 December 2025.
17706063.brief: Angling Direct repurchased 60,000 shares at 48p per share on 24 July 2026, continuing its extended buyback programme.
17706063.take: Routine treasury share purchase; signals management confidence in valuation but immaterial to retail investors. Standard capital management activity with no operational or financial substance.

17706067.summary: Forgent plc announced successful Phase 1 drilling results from Peak Hill Gold-Copper Project in Western Australia, with 40 aircore holes (2,680m) completed in July 2026. Key intercepts include 2m @ 3.68g/t Au and multiple other gold hits validating the company's geological model. A previously undrilled exploration corridor between Junction and Curley's prospects has been identified with favourable structural and magnetic characteristics. Phase 2 drilling, focusing on extending mineralization and testing the new corridor, is scheduled to commence August 2026, with advancement towards an initial Mineral Resource Estimate planned.
17706067.brief: Forgent's Peak Hill gold project delivers encouraging assay results from maiden drilling, identifying significant new exploration corridor.
17706067.take: Positive catalyst: de-risked exploration model, multiple confirmed gold systems, and new high-priority target materially expand project potential, supporting near-term drilling activity and value discovery.

17706064.summary: Literacy Capital's NAV per share decreased to 472.6p from 481.3p at Q1 2026, reflecting challenging conditions for smaller UK businesses. Q2 saw £20.6m cash inflows from Wifinity and fund interest sales, offset by £13.3m invested in bolt-on acquisitions and portfolio support. RCI Group and Grayce, previous NAV detractors, showed positive momentum; Red Sky and Trinitatum posted strong returns (5.8x and 4.3x money multiples respectively). The fund drew £8.7m on its £40m revolving credit facility and retained £0.7m cash. Management highlighted weak NAV performance historically but expects portfolio momentum to improve valuations.
17706064.brief: Literacy Capital NAV fell 1.8% to 472.6p in Q2 2026 amid difficult UK market conditions, though recent exits generated £20.6m cash inflows.
17706064.take: Mixed signals: solid cash generation and some portfolio improvements offset by NAV decline and broader UK SME headwinds. Market likely sees this as holding pattern pending turnaround evidence; Main Market listing aspiration suggests management recognises NAV discount problem.

17706065.summary: AdvancedAdvT Limited purchased 47,500 ordinary shares at 170.0 pence per share on 24 July 2026, bringing cumulative buyback total to 5,340,500 shares. Shares are held in treasury. Following the purchase, total voting rights stand at 131,785,306 shares. The buyback programme was originally announced on 4 March 2026.
17706065.brief: AdvancedAdvT continues share buyback, purchasing 47,500 shares at 170p on 24 July.
17706065.take: Routine capital management activity; share buybacks typically indicate management confidence in valuation but have limited impact on share price trajectory without broader strategic catalysts.

17706069.summary: Hiscox completed share buybacks totalling 334,711 ordinary shares between 20-24 July 2026 via Peel Hunt, with daily volumes ranging from 64,122 to 68,252 shares. Prices ranged from 1,794p to 1,864p per share, with a blended average of approximately 1,835p. The shares will be cancelled. This forms part of the buyback programme announced on 25 February 2026.
17706069.brief: Hiscox repurchased 334,711 shares at 1,814p average price during 20-24 July as part of ongoing buyback programme.
17706069.take: Routine capital management activity signalling confidence in valuation; shareholders benefit from reduced share count but represents non-event for near-term trading.

17706068.summary: Dianomi PLC posted H1 2026 revenues of £13.4m (H1 2025: £13.2m), up 2% YoY or 4.5% on constant currency. Gross profit improved to £3.9m with margin of 28.9% versus 25.3% prior year. The Group expects a small EBITDA loss, substantially better than H1 2025's £0.6m loss. Cash position strengthened to £6.0m with positive cash flow despite EBITDA loss and zero debt. Key developments include expanded partnerships with CNN News and Associated Press, launch of Dianomi Interactive ad format in April, and a new dedicated Investor Relations vertical.
17706068.brief: Dianomi reports H1 2026 revenue growth of 2% with significantly improved margins and near-breakeven EBITDA.
17706068.take: Modest headline growth masked by strong margin expansion and operational improvement signals early recovery; new product traction and publisher expansion validate platform strength, though cautious advertiser spending indicates cyclical headwinds persist.

17706070.summary: Plus500 purchased 15,454 ordinary shares on 24 July 2026 through Panmure Liberum Limited at prices ranging from 3,980p to 4,076p, with volume-weighted average price of 4,018.80p. Shares will be held in treasury. Following the purchase, 68.9 million shares remain in issue (excluding treasury) with company holding 46 million treasury shares. Total voting rights stand at 68.9 million.
17706070.brief: Plus500 repurchased 15,454 shares on 24 July at average price of 4,018.80p under existing buyback programme.
17706070.take: Routine capital allocation activity under disclosed buyback programme. Treasury share purchases are non-dilutive but market typically views buybacks neutral to slightly positive as disciplined capital management.

17706089.summary: FY25 group revenue reached £73.8m (up 8.5% YoY) with system sales of £98.3m. UK like-for-like sales grew 6.2%, significantly outperforming the CGA benchmark's -1.3% decline. H1 2026 trading accelerated materially post-expansion to multi-aggregator delivery (Deliveroo, Uber Eats, Just Eat), with UK LFL sales reaching +19.7% and delivery surging +54.1%. Adjusted EBITDA (pre-IFRS 16) was £1.1m (UK: £6.3m; France: -£5.2m loss). Accounting issues in France reduced EBITDA by £2.7m with no cash impact. System sales exceeded £100m milestone in June 2026. Founder Brandon Stephens returned as Group CEO in February 2026; new Chair Duncan Garrood appointed.
17706089.brief: Tortilla reports FY25 revenue of £73.8m (+8.5%) with UK momentum accelerating; France accounting issues resolved.
17706089.take: Strong UK trading recovery and multi-aggregator expansion driving material acceleration offset by France's ongoing challenges and prior accounting weakness; market likely positive on UK momentum but cautious on France turnaround credibility and governance reset.

17706072.summary: Helios Underwriting purchased 128,490 ordinary shares (10p each) via Peel Hunt between 20-24 July 2026 at prices ranging from 222.0p to 224.8p, with a weighted average of 223.24p. 17706072.brief: Helios Underwriting repurchased 128,490 shares at 222-224.8p between 20-24 July, placing them in Treasury.
17706072.take: Routine share buyback execution under previously announced programme; modest capital management activity typical for insurance investment companies; neutral signal with no material impact.

17706074.brief: Ryanair bought back 280,755 shares in week of 20-24 July 2026 for cancellation under existing programme.
17706074.take: Routine capital allocation activity signalling management confidence in valuation; continuation of existing programme presents non-event for markets absent material changes to buyback scope or pace.

17706075.summary: AstraZeneca reported H1 2026 total revenue of $30.7bn (+6% at constant exchange rates), with product revenue up 6% to $30.6bn. Core EPS grew 11% to $5.21. Oncology and Rare Disease delivered double-digit growth, offsetting Farxiga US loss of exclusivity and China volume-based procurement headwinds. Company reconfirms FY 2026 guidance: mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth and low double-digit core EPS growth. 30 regulatory approvals achieved since Q4 2025; 6 positive Phase III trials completed. Interim dividend increased 3 cents to $1.06 per share. Two acquisition agreements announced: Dizal Pharmaceutical ($600m upfront for Zegfrovy) and Sino Biopharmaceutical ($200m upfront for TQC3721).
17706075.brief: AstraZeneca H1 2026: 6% revenue growth, 11% core EPS growth, on track for $80bn 2030 ambition.
17706075.take: Solid execution meeting expectations with strong oncology/rare disease performance offsetting known near-term headwinds; pipeline momentum and acquisition strategy signal confidence in long-term 2030 goals, though China weakness and generic pressures persist.

17706076.summary: Serica Energy has agreed to acquire Pharos Energy for 28.67p cash per share plus 4p special dividend (32.67p total), valuing the company at £145.7m. This represents a 20.7% premium to the Ratio Offer's 27.07p consideration and 28.6% above the undisturbed closing price of 25.4p on 23 June 2026. The acquisition adds cash-generative production in Vietnam and Egypt, increasing pro forma 2P reserves by 13% to 156.8 mmboe and expected 2026 exit production to 70,000 boepd. Completion expected H1 2027, subject to regulatory approvals in Vietnam and Egypt.
17706076.brief: Serica Energy to acquire Pharos Energy for 32.67p per share in cash, representing 20.7% premium to rival Ratio offer.
17706076.take: Positive signal for oil/gas M&A market; demonstrates disciplined capital deployment at $8.4/2P boe valuation with clear strategic fit and near-term accretion. Successful competing bid validates market conditions for energy sector consolidation.

17706077.summary: Vertu Motors completed purchases of 166,551 ordinary shares between 20-24 July 2026 at prices ranging from 78.0p to 79.25p, with shares to be cancelled. Post-cancellation, total voting shares stand at 310,730,236. Since July 2017, the company has returned £47.7m to shareholders through buybacks, reducing shares in issue by 21.8%. Purchases were executed through Shore Capital Stockbrokers under the buyback programme announced 5 March 2026.
17706077.brief: Vertu Motors repurchased 166,551 shares at 78-79p in ongoing buyback programme.
17706077.take: Routine capital allocation update; share buybacks typically neutral-to-modest positive signal of management confidence, though announcement provides no fresh insight into trading conditions or strategic direction.

17706078.summary: Revenue secured or highly advanced for FY26 stands at £34m versus £40m last year, with £5.5m shifted to H2 and £5m delayed to FY27 due to project delays. Middle East revenue hit £11.5m (35% higher than FY25's £8.5m), while IP revenues reached £2.2m of expected £3.4m FY26. Cash position fell to £2.7m from £4.2m, reflecting earn-out payments, restructuring costs, and working capital timing. Three strategic growth pillars on track; Group completed £700k of £1m annualised cost-saving target. WMP Qatar acquisition awaiting completion due to Qatari mourning period.
17706078.brief: Zinc Media reports H1 FY26 trading update showing £34m revenue secured for FY26 (down from £40m prior year) with strong Middle East growth offsetting market headwinds.
17706078.take: Mixed signals: strong underlying growth in priority segments (Middle East, IP, genre) and cost discipline offset near-term revenue decline and working capital pressure, creating cautious sentiment on near-term momentum but confidence in medium-term strategy.

17706079.summary: Pets at Home Group executed 980,000 share buybacks between 20-24 July 2026 via Deutsche Bank at weighted average prices ranging 195.6-198.7p per share. Total shares in issue reduced to 444,052,022 with no treasury shares held. Shares will be cancelled. Purchase prices ranged from 192.9p (lowest) to 199.7p (highest). Programme was announced 24 June 2026.
17706079.brief: Pets at Home repurchased 980,000 shares at average price 197.1p during week of 20-24 July as part of approved buyback programme.
17706079.take: Routine capital management activity; share buybacks typically viewed as neutral to mildly positive, signalling confidence in valuation but offering no material strategic insight.

17706080.summary: Zephyr Energy signed a non-binding Letter of Intent with Atlas Oil for a Prepaid Commodity Purchase Agreement providing up to US$15 million in non-dilutive financing for the Paradox project in Utah. Funds support infrastructure build-out, well workovers, and gas processing facilities, with repayment from future production sales. Atlas, which has marketed Zephyr's oil since 2021, gains exclusive hydrocarbon marketing rights during a specified term. Closing expected Q3-Q4 2026, contingent on binding definitive agreements and due diligence. No equity dilution or asset-level working interest sale occurs.
17706080.brief: Zephyr Energy secures up to US$15m non-dilutive pre-production financing from Atlas Oil for Paradox Basin project.
17706080.take: Positive signal: established industry partner's confidence in Paradox asset via structured capital; non-dilutive financing preserves shareholder equity while funding pre-production phase, though LOI remains non-binding pending Q4 completion.

17706081.summary: UK food producer Cranswick reported Q1 revenue 5.5% ahead of prior year (like-for-like +4.0%) with volume growth of 8.2% (like-for-like +6.4%). Poultry revenue grew strongly from capacity expansion at Eye facility and new retail business onboarding. Pet Products revenue significantly outperformed, reflecting Pets at Home partnership expansion. Export revenue declined due to weak China demand. The company formed a joint venture with The Jolly Hog Group and continues major capital deployment including 25% capacity increase at Eye and Hull pork facility expansion. Net debt remained in line with March 2026 year-end; FY27 outlook remains aligned with market expectations (£230-243m adjusted PBT range).
17706081.brief: Cranswick posts strong Q1 with 5.5% revenue growth and 8.2% volume uplift driven by poultry expansion and pet products.
17706081.take: Positive momentum on volume-led growth and margin accretion from input cost reductions, offset somewhat by export headwinds. Maintained FY guidance suggests confidence despite geopolitical risks; significant capex deployment indicates management conviction in longer-term returns.

17706082.summary: Oracle Power's consultants Resources WA completed studies for the Northern Zone Kalgoorlie Gold Project in Western Australia. Key findings: waste rock is non-acid forming with minimal acid mine drainage risk; geotechnical assessments show high safety factors for waste dumps and pit slopes (>1.33); groundwater table sits 37 metres below surface with low permeability and unlikely material operational risk; flood modelling suggests only minor infrastructure required. The Native Vegetation Clearing Permit is in final stages with submission expected within weeks; the Mine Development and Closure Plan is 60% complete and on schedule.
17706082.brief: Oracle Power reports positive environmental and geotechnical studies for Kalgoorlie Gold Project permit applications.
17706082.take: Positive read: removal of major environmental and technical barriers accelerates path to mining permits and operations, de-risking the project significantly for investors seeking near-term commodity exposure.

17706083.summary: All eight resolutions passed at Team Internet's 2026 AGM held 24 July with majority support. Financial statements approved 100%, director re-elections backed 94-99%, share allotment authority 83.45%, and share buyback authority 99.97%. Remuneration report received 77.50% support, prompting board commitment to ongoing shareholder engagement on pay policy. Voting participation was strong with 172.7m votes cast across resolutions.
17706083.brief: Team Internet Group passes all AGM resolutions with strong shareholder support on 24 July 2026.
17706083.take: Routine governance approval with robust support across all measures. Remuneration opposition (22.5%) merits monitoring but represents improving trend; buyback authority approval signals capital management flexibility. Non-event for most investors.

17706084.summary: EKF Diagnostics Holdings plc completed a share buyback on 24 July 2026, purchasing 60,000 ordinary shares at a weighted average price of 25.1932 pence per share. The shares will be cancelled. Following the cancellation, total issued share capital will comprise 429,913,112 ordinary shares with no treasury holdings. The transaction was executed on AIM (AIMX) at 09:02:31.
17706084.brief: EKF Diagnostics repurchases 60,000 shares at 25.19p for cancellation, reducing issued capital to 429.9m shares.
17706084.take: Routine capital management action signalling confidence in valuation, though modest scale suggests limited material impact on earnings per share accretion or shareholder value creation.

17706085.summary: Tritax Big Box REIT has obtained planning consent for a 107MW data centre facility on its 74-acre Manor Farm site in Slough following successful conclusion of a judicial review. The company has secured an accelerated power delivery pathway and a pre-let agreement following competitive marketing. The facility is expected to achieve a 9.3% yield on cost upon completion, with rental income commencing post-practical completion. Planning consent represents a key de-risking milestone expected to drive capital profit recognition in early development phases.
17706085.brief: Tritax Big Box secures planning consent for 107MW data centre at Manor Farm in Slough, unlocking significant value creation.
17706085.take: Positive read: planning approval removes a major hurdle in a supply-constrained market, secured power access de-risks execution, and pre-letting demonstrates occupier demand supporting the 9.3% yield target.

17706086.summary: Mendell Helium PLC has entered a settlement agreement with a former broker whereby the broker will exercise warrants over 500,000 new ordinary shares at 3 pence per share. Following admission of these shares on 31 July 2026, the Company's total voting rights will be 341,886,938 ordinary shares.
17706086.brief: Mendell Helium settles broker dispute via 500,000 share issuance at 3p per share, offsetting £15,000 obligation.
17706086.take: Routine settlement resolution with modest dilution (0.15% share increase); demonstrates dispute resolution but raises questions about historical broker obligations and governance.

17706087.summary: AOTI achieved $35m revenue in H1 2026 (10% YoY growth; 18% underlying), with net debt of $6.3m and cash of $13.8m. VA revenues (57% of total) grew 15% YoY, while Medicaid (41%) grew 21% on underlying basis. Post-period, CMS published a proposed Local Coverage Determination affirming Medicare coverage for topical oxygen therapy treating diabetic foot ulcers nationwide, with final determination expected within 12 months. Management expects this will dramatically expand the addressable market and accelerate TWO2® therapy adoption across Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial segments.
17706087.brief: AOTI reports 10% H1 revenue growth to $35m; CMS proposes Medicare coverage for topical oxygen therapy, a transformational milestone.
17706087.take: Market likely views this positively: robust underlying growth trajectory exceeding guidance, plus the proposed CMS Medicare LCD represents a significant regulatory de-risking catalyst that could materially unlock US market expansion, though near-term revenue impact remains contingent on final determination.

17706071.summary: iFOREX delivered H1 2026 revenue of approximately $27.0m (H1 2025: $27.6m), with adjusted EBITDA of $4.2m on constant currency basis but only $2.4m reported due to exceptional ILS strengthening. Client metrics improved: 19% new onboarding increase, 8% active client growth, though ARPU declined 9% versus H1 2025. The company maintains $12m net cash, no debt, and formally submitted a UAE Category 5 licence application. Full-year operational costs expected $2m higher than anticipated due to persistent FX headwinds.
17706071.brief: iFOREX reports H1 2026 revenue of $27.0m, flat YoY but up 25% versus H2 2025; FX headwinds cited.
17706071.take: Underlying business resilience offset by material FX translation headwinds; regulatory progress and leadership appointments signal growth ambitions, but cautious FX outlook suggests near-term margin pressure.

17706092.summary: Vesuvius reports H1 2026 trading profit of approximately £74m. The Steel division continues experiencing operational issues, while Advanced Refractories faces challenging conditions in Europe. These problems are temporary but have greater impact than previously guided; expected resolution by year-end. Full-year trading profit now forecast slightly ahead of FY25 on a constant currency basis (FY25 constant currency trading profit: £147m). Half-year results announcement scheduled for 30 July 2026.
17706092.brief: Vesuvius expects H1 2026 trading profit of £74m; full-year profit slightly ahead of FY25 on constant currency basis, but operational issues worse than anticipated.
17706092.take: Downgrade from previous expectations despite maintained full-year guidance suggests operational headwinds are material; market likely focused on whether management's timeline for resolution is credible.

17706090.summary: Vodafone delivered Q1 FY27 organic service revenue growth of 5.2% with 6.2% organic Adjusted EBITDAaL growth to €2.9bn. All segments grew including Germany (1.2%), UK (0.6%), and Africa (12.6%). Following completion of the Safaricom acquisition on 30 June 2026, Vodafone updated FY27 guidance with Group Adjusted EBITDAaL expected €13.0-13.3bn and Adjusted free cash flow €2.6-2.9bn, now expecting to deliver the upper end of ranges. Safaricom contributes €1.1bn EBITDA impact over nine months.
17706090.brief: Vodafone reports strong Q1 start with 5.2% organic service revenue growth and 6.2% EBITDA growth; raises FY27 guidance after Safaricom acquisition.
17706090.take: Strong Q1 execution with accelerating business segment growth (5.0%) and margin expansion suggest the turnaround strategy is gaining traction; upgraded guidance and expectation to deliver upper end signals management confidence, likely supporting sentiment.

17706050.brief: AEP Plantations repurchased 56,179 shares on 24 July at 171-178p as part of its ongoing buyback programme.

17706051.brief: Frasers Group repurchased 206,831 shares between 20-24 July 2026 at an average of 752.6p, adding to treasury holdings.
17706051.take: Routine capital allocation activity signalling management confidence in valuation; modest buyback scale suggests disciplined capital deployment but insufficient to materially move shareholder value or EPS.

17706053.brief: Helios Towers bought back 600,000 shares at average 195.76p per share during 20-24 July, to be cancelled.
17706053.take: Share cancellations reduce share count, supporting EPS mechanically. Market likely views as neutral-to-mildly-positive shareholder return, though modest scale relative to total capitalisation suggests incremental rather than transformative.

17706054.summary: Engineering recruitment group RTC Group delivered H1 2026 revenue of £45.2m (H1 2025: £48.3m) with profit from operations of £0.8m (2025: £1.3m). Gross margin held steady at 18.3% despite fuel cost inflation. The company generated £0.9m operating cash inflow, maintains £3.8m cash with no term debt, and proposes an interim dividend of 1.21p per share (maintained from prior year). Six significant contract wins secured across divisions, with strong order book. Key headwinds cited: elevated fuel costs from geopolitical tensions, soft UK recruitment market, smart metering transition, and government employment cost increases.
17706054.brief: RTC Group reports H1 2026 interim results showing revenue decline to £45.2m and profit fall to £0.8m amid cost pressures.
17706054.take: Deteriorating H1 results and cautious forward guidance signal near-term operational stress, though maintained dividend and zero debt provide downside protection; market likely views this as cyclically challenged but structurally sound, pending infrastructure spending recovery.

17706055.summary: Oakley Capital Investments Limited purchased 100,000 ordinary shares at 508 pence per share on 24 July 2026 for cancellation under its capital allocation policy. 17706055.brief: OCI repurchases 100,000 shares at 508p each for cancellation, reducing shares in issue to 164.6m.
17706055.take: Routine capital management action demonstrating shareholder-friendly capital deployment; modest share count reduction supports per-share metrics but represents minor transaction relative to total capitalisation.

17706056.summary: Vehicle tracking software firm Quartix reported revenue of £19.4m (up 12% YoY), profit before tax of £4.8m (up 21%), and EBITDA of £7.2m (up 16%) for H1 2026. Annualised recurring revenue grew 11% to £38.9m, with subscription base expanding 7% to 342,679 units. Free cash flow increased 18% to £3.0m. The company maintained net cash of £4.8m and proposed an interim dividend of 2.70p per share. Gross margin improved to 80% from 78.4%, aided by hardware cost reductions and pricing discipline. Management expects to meet full-year market expectations for revenue, adjusted EBIT, and free cash flow.
17706056.brief: Quartix posts strong H1 2026 results with 12% revenue growth to £19.4m and 21% profit growth; proposes 2.70p interim dividend.
17706056.take: Solid operational execution with strong recurring revenue model showing 11% ARR growth, margin expansion, and improved cash generation; however, diluted EPS fell to 5.51p (from 6.50p) due to prior-year tax adjustments, which may temper near-term sentiment despite fundamentals improving.

17706057.summary: SSP Group PLC purchased 1,150,000 ordinary shares for cancellation between 20-24 July 2026 from Barclays Bank plc, paying between 180.90p and 191.90p per share with a volume-weighted average price of 187.06p. Following cancellation, outstanding ordinary shares reduce to 761,393,550, representing the total voting rights in the company. All purchases were executed on-exchange via the London Stock Exchange.
17706057.brief: SSP Group repurchased 1.15m shares at avg 187.06p in week of 20-24 July under £100m buyback programme.
17706057.take: Routine capital management execution; buyback progresses on schedule at reasonable valuations near programme average, implying management confidence but representing non-event for sentiment.

17706058.summary: Estadio Gana hosted 13 World Cup matches in Mexico, achieving significant growth metrics: daily betting activity peaked at 162% above early June levels, client registrations grew 136% to exceed 40,000 by 24 July 2026, and Gross Gaming Revenues increased 227%. Mexican National Team fixtures drove bookmaker activity. First-time World Cup players are converting to long-term users across MLB, Liga MX, Tennis, UFC and La Liga. CEO Mark Epstein highlighted Q3 2026 as a period of significant growth potential.
17706058.brief: Gana Media's Estadio Gana sports betting platform reports strong World Cup performance with 136% client registration growth and 227% GGR increase.
17706058.take: Strong operational metrics from a major sporting event validate Estadio Gana's customer acquisition strategy and user retention, suggesting positive momentum into Q3 despite World Cup-driven volatility being temporary.

17706046.summary: Celebrus Technologies PLC purchased 20,706 ordinary shares on 24 July 2026 at a volume-weighted average price of 108.28 pence per share through Cavendish Capital Markets. The shares will be held in treasury. Following this transaction, the company has 40,431,453 shares in issue with 2,646,335 held in treasury, resulting in 37,785,118 voting rights.
17706046.brief: Celebrus Technologies repurchases 20,706 shares at 108.28p per share for treasury.
17706046.take: Routine share buyback signalling modest capital management; modest scale suggests non-event for investors unless part of broader return-of-capital programme.

17706045.brief: Melrose Industries repurchased 31,000 shares at 463-479p over five days, adding to 65.4m treasury shares.

17706043.brief: Prudential repurchased 1.58m shares in week of 20-24 July 2026 at 10.45-11.21p; 48.97m shares cancelled YTD.
17706043.take: Routine capital allocation activity under shareholder-approved authority; buybacks at current valuations neutral to slightly positive for remaining shareholders through EPS accretion, though immaterial to fundamentals.

Following this transaction, the company now holds 1,225,611 shares in treasury with 117,481,200 shares in issue. The purchases form part of a buyback programme announced 8 June 2026.
17706061.brief: Helical repurchases 239,738 shares at 195-198p as part of June buyback programme; now holds 1.23m treasury shares.

Following cancellation, issued share capital stands at 155,590,790 ordinary shares with total voting rights of 155,590,790.
17706007.brief: Macfarlane Group completes share buyback, purchasing 59,920 shares at 68-71p for cancellation.
17706007.take: Routine share buyback execution under existing programme; modest scale suggests measured capital return; buyback at current market prices indicates management confidence but represents incremental EPS accretion only.

17706006.summary: VinaCapital Vietnam Opportunity Fund Limited repurchased 15,539 USD ordinary shares on 24 July 2026 at GBP 4.175938 per share, to be held as treasury shares. Total treasury shares now stand at 6,793,681, with 120,285,842 shares in issue. The total voting rights in the Company remain 120,285,842 shares.
17706006.brief: VinaCapital Vietnam Opportunity Fund repurchased 15,539 shares at GBP 4.18 on 24 July 2026.
17706006.take: Routine share buyback with modest volume; standard capital management action with no material implications for fund positioning or strategy.

17706005.summary: The PR technology company achieved H1 2026 revenue of US$7.3 million (up 14% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of US$1.7 million (up 31% YoY), with cash receipts up 80% despite 4% bad debts. Repeat customer revenue rose to 36% from 16%, and the company secured a landmark US$0.7 million contract. Net cash stood at US$5.9 million. Investments in sales team management, APAC expansion, and AI tools (Pressella achieving 7x human success rate) position the business for H2 growth, with FY 2026 guidance of US$14.0m revenue and US$4.0m Adjusted EBITDA expected to be met.
17706005.brief: Pathos Communications reports 14% revenue growth to US$7.3m and 31% Adjusted EBITDA growth to US$1.7m in H1 2026.
17706005.take: Strong operational execution post-IPO with impressive cash conversion and margin expansion despite growth investments, supported by strategic partnerships and AI advancement; suggests management delivering on growth strategy and positioning well for FY guidance.

17706004.summary: CVS Group purchased 189,802 ordinary shares between 20-24 July 2026 at prices ranging from 1,182p to 1,308p, with a volume-weighted average of 1,265.49p. 17706004.brief: CVS Group completes share buyback of 189,802 shares at 1,265.49p average price; 1.6m shares repurchased to date under programme.
17706004.take: Routine capital management activity; share cancellation reduces share count marginally, potentially supporting per-share metrics. Prices paid suggest stock traded in mid-1,200p range during the period, with modest weakness by 24 July.

17706343.summary: FirstGroup purchased 2,774,467 ordinary shares through RBC Europe Limited between 20-24 July 2026 at weighted average prices ranging from 177.44p to 181.43p daily. Buyback programme was announced on 18 June 2026.
17706343.brief: FirstGroup bought back 2.77m shares at 172.8p-182.8p during July 20-24 under its announced buyback programme.
17706343.take: Routine capital management activity signalling confidence in valuation; buybacks typically neutral-to-slightly positive as they support EPS and reduce share count, though execution at rising prices (172-182p range) suggests disciplined approach.

17706335.brief: BlackRock Smaller Companies Trust updates voting rights denominator to 244.3m shares excluding treasury holdings.

17706330.brief: BlackRock Greater Europe Investment Trust updates voting rights denominator to 90.3m shares.
17706330.take: Routine disclosure of voting rights denominator; no material implications for investors or share price. Standard regulatory housekeeping for investment trusts.

17706351.summary: QBT has received formal approval from the US Patent and Trademark Office for its 'Message Scheduling for Cryptographic Hashing' patent application (US No. 18/696,073). The ASIC UltraBoost invention aims to improve Bitcoin mining efficiency by eliminating redundant SHA256 message schedule computations. Final patent grant remains subject to formalities including payment of issue and publication fees. CEO Francesco Gardin stated the company is seeking semiconductor sector advisers to explore monetisation opportunities through licensing or commercial arrangements, with no assurance of near-term material revenue.
17706351.brief: Quantum Blockchain Technologies receives US patent approval for ASIC Ultra Boost, a Bitcoin mining efficiency technology.
17706351.take: Early-stage IP portfolio development with potential licensing upside, though monetisation timeline and scale remain highly uncertain; modest positive for long-term optionality but not material near-term catalyst.

17706348.summary: Ashoka WhiteOak Emerging Markets Trust returned 24.49% in Q2 2026, beating the MSCI EM index's 23.3% gain. Top performers included SK Hynix (+222.6%), MediaTek (+184.1%), and Elite Material (+106.7%), while Tencent (-10.8%) and Laopu Gold (-43.7%) lagged. The portfolio's top 10 holdings (39.6% of NAV) are dominated by Taiwan and South Korea semiconductors: TSMC (11.4%), Samsung Electronics (9.2%), and SK Hynix (8.3%). EM markets significantly outperformed US equities (S&P 500: 14.8%) and MSCI World (13.5%).
17706348.brief: AWEM delivered 24.49% return in Q2 2026, outperforming benchmark by 1.24% on strong semiconductor and tech holdings.
17706348.take: Strong Q2 performance driven by EM semiconductor strength suggests effective manager stock-picking; outperformance validates the performance-fee model alignment, though concentration in cyclical tech stocks carries execution risk.

17706358.summary: Anglesey Mining plc has confirmed James McFarlane as Principal Geologist on a retained basis. McFarlane is a Chartered Geologist and Chartered Engineer with over 20 years' international experience in mineral exploration, resource evaluation, and mining operations, with specific expertise in volcanogenic massive sulphide deposits and UK mine development. He will lead geological interpretation, guide future Mineral Resource updates, support economic reassessment of the Parys Mountain Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag-Au VMS project, and mentor the company's recently appointed Exploration Geologist.
17706358.brief: Anglesey Mining appoints James McFarlane as Principal Geologist to advance Parys Mountain polymetallic project.
17706358.take: Appointment of an experienced technical leader signals management commitment to advancing the UK's largest polymetallic VMS project; likely read as positive for project development momentum.

17706356.summary: Bodycote plc purchased 130,000 ordinary shares for cancellation during 20-24 July 2026 via Barclays Bank at prices ranging from 685.00p to 706.00p, with a volume-weighted average of 697.38p. Since programme commencement, 2,394,016 shares have been repurchased. Post-cancellation, 170,368,574 shares remain in issue. The purchases are part of the first £40m tranche of an £80m total buyback scheme announced 11 March 2026.
17706356.brief: Bodycote repurchased 130,000 shares at 685-706p in week of 20-24 July as part of £80m buyback programme.
17706356.take: Routine capital return signalling management confidence in valuation; buyback programmes are generally shareholder-neutral on fundamentals but reduce share count, supporting EPS. Market typically views as mild positive or non-event depending on pricing and equity opportunity cost.

17706357.summary: BlackRock American Income Trust plc notified the market of its voting rights position as at 27 July 2026 under FCA Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules 5.6.1. The company has 61,960,138 ordinary shares in issue, each carrying one vote per share, with an additional 33,401,167 ordinary shares held in treasury. 17706357.brief: BlackRock American Income Trust updates total voting rights; 61.96m ordinary shares in issue as at 27 July 2026.
17706357.take: Routine disclosure of voting capital structure required under FCA rules; no material implications for investors or market-moving information.

17706884.summary: Bytes Technology Group PLC repurchased 250,000 ordinary shares between 22-24 July 2026 via Peel Hunt at prices ranging from 414.0p to 420.0p. 17706884.brief: Bytes Technology repurchased 250,000 shares at 414-420p during week of 20-24 July under existing buyback programme.
17706884.take: Routine share buyback execution within previously announced programme; signals management confidence in valuation but represents incremental capital allocation rather than material shareholder news.

17706879.summary: Jyske Bank executed 56,137 share repurchases during week 30 (20-24 July 2026) at an average price of DKK 1,010.37, totalling DKK 56.7m. Since the programme's February 2026 launch, the bank has acquired 1,584,918 treasury shares worth DKK 1.456bn against a DKK 3bn authorisation, representing 2.72% of share capital. All transactions occurred on Nasdaq Copenhagen under Market Abuse Regulation Safe Harbour provisions.
17706879.brief: Jyske Bank repurchased 56,137 shares in week 30 2026, bringing total buyback to 1.58m shares (2.72% of capital).
17706879.take: Routine capital management execution within authorised parameters. Steady buyback progression (49% of budget deployed) signals ongoing shareholder return focus; modest weekly volumes suggest measured, compliant execution with no material implications.

17706387.summary: AstraZeneca's Ultomiris (ravulizumab) did not achieve statistical significance for event-free survival at 26 weeks versus placebo in adults and adolescents with HSCT-TMA (haematopoietic stem cell transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy). However, the paediatric Phase III trial (ALXN1210-TMA-314) showed clinically meaningful overall survival of 87.2% at 26 weeks and 73.4% at 52 weeks. The company is advancing regulatory filings for paediatric patients based on these results and external control data. Discussions with health authorities continue regarding adult indication interpretation with real-world evidence.
17706387.brief: Ultomiris fails primary endpoint in adult HSCT-TMA trial but shows promise in pediatric patients; regulatory filings advancing for children.
17706387.take: Mixed results dampen near-term prospects for adult indication but preserve paediatric pathway; narrow market (fewer than 6,000 US patients) limits commercial upside regardless; likely non-event for broader stock given limited revenue potential.

17706888.summary: Railways Pension Trustee Company Limited (Railpen) announced on 27 July 2026 it will not make an offer for IP Group plc, ending a potential acquisition process. The Board granted a PUSU deadline extension to assess proposals but could not reach mutually acceptable terms. IP Group's Board expresses confidence in its strategy, highlighting anticipated value-accretive milestones over 18 months, strong portfolio progress, third-party capital platform expansion, and disciplined capital allocation. The company is no longer in an "offer period" under City Code rules.
17706888.brief: Railpen confirms no takeover bid for IP Group; Rule 2.8 restrictions now apply.
17706888.take: Failed takeover process ends with target company reaffirming strategic confidence; modest positive for those bullish on standalone execution strategy, neutral-to-negative for those preferred the Railpen alternative.

17706889.summary: Gelion plc submitted its regulatory block admission return for the period ending 26 July 2026 covering its existing share option plan. No additional listings occurred.
17706889.brief: Gelion reports block admission return for share option plan covering 26 January to 26 July 2026.
17706889.take: Routine regulatory disclosure showing no share option activity over the six-month period; no material implications for shareholders or stock price.

17706902.summary: Balfour Beatty purchased 452,462 ordinary shares between 20-24 July 2026 through Merrill Lynch International at a volume weighted average price of 803.5171 pence, to be held in treasury. Since the programme's launch in January 2026 and expansion in March, the group has now repurchased 14.67 million shares. Following this purchase, 478.27 million ordinary shares remain in issue (excluding treasury shares), which represents the total voting rights denominator for disclosure purposes.
17706902.brief: Balfour Beatty repurchases 452,462 shares at average 803.5p as part of ongoing buyback programme.
17706902.take: Routine execution of pre-announced buyback programme; no strategic implications or surprises. Share repurchases are capital management tool; generally neutral unless price trajectory raises capital allocation concerns.

17706893.summary: LSL Property Services purchased 102,000 ordinary shares on LSL between 20-24 July 2026 via Shore Capital at volume-weighted average prices ranging from 230.795p to 242.07p per share. The buyback forms part of the programme announced 27 January 2026. Following the repurchase, the company holds 5.87 million treasury shares and has 99.29 million shares in issue with voting rights, from a total issued capital of 105.16 million shares.
17706893.brief: LSL Property Services repurchased 102,000 shares (20-24 July) at 230-242p as part of ongoing buyback programme.
17706893.take: Routine share buyback execution under existing programme; suggests management confidence in valuation but represents capital allocation rather than strategic news. Market likely to view as neutral housekeeping activity.

17706897.summary: FirstGroup plc has completed the first tranche of its £100m on-market share buyback programme announced 18 June 2026. RBC Europe Limited purchased 13,553,662 ordinary shares for £24.8m, now held in Treasury. Panmure Liberum Limited has commenced the second £25m tranche effective 27 July 2026, with remaining tranches expected to proceed as originally scheduled.
17706897.brief: FirstGroup completes first £24.8m tranche of £100m buyback; second £25m tranche now underway.
17706897.take: Routine capital management signalling confidence in valuation; buybacks typically neutral-to-positive but non-material unless capital constraints emerge or share price deteriorates significantly.

17706906.summary: Cambridge Cognition (AIM: COG) posted H1 2026 revenues of £5.0m, up 16% year-on-year, including first healthcare and consumer wellness pilot revenues of £0.1m. Contracted orders underpin minimum £10.0m FY2026 revenue with six months selling remaining. The company reported adjusted EBITDA loss of £0.3m (vs £0.4m loss H1 2025), positive operational cash flow, and reduced borrowings from £0.9m to £0.2m. In July, Cambridge Cognition completed a £2.5m placing and fully repaid debt, achieving debt-free status. The board remains confident in meeting consensus forecasts of £11.35m FY2026 revenue and £1.25m adjusted LBT.
17706906.brief: Cambridge Cognition reports 16% H1 revenue growth to £5.0m; confident in FY2026 guidance after July fundraising and debt clearance.
17706906.take: Positive momentum: revenue growth acceleration, debt elimination, new market expansion (healthcare/wellness), and equity fundraising support strategic investment programmes expected to drive growth from 2028. Board confidence aligns with market expectations.

17706913.summary: Hellenic Telecomms Organization S.A. repurchased 222,509 shares between 20-24 July 2026 at an average price of €19.66, spending €4.37 million total. The company now holds 1,600,038 treasury shares representing 0.406% of outstanding shares. Share prices ranged from €19.40 to €20.00 across the five trading days.
17706913.brief: OTE purchased 222,509 own shares during 20-24 July 2026 for €4.37m as part of its 2026 buyback programme.
17706913.take: Share buyback signals management confidence in valuation and capital allocation flexibility; typically neutral to slightly positive, though markets focus more on execution versus strategic alternatives.

17706912.summary: Yellow Cake's uranium inventory grew from 23.1m lb to 23.2m lb following 100,000 lb spot purchase in April 2026. Company exercised 2026 option to buy 1.16m lb from Kazatomprom at US$86.15/lb (US$100m) for H2 2026 delivery, raising post-delivery holdings to 24.4m lb. NAV per share increased 0.2% to £6.34 (31 March: £6.33), reflecting uranium holdings valuation rise to US$1,969.7m offset by sterling appreciation. Completed US$10m share buyback programme purchasing 1.36m shares at 544.41p average price.
17706912.brief: Yellow Cake reports Q2 2026 uranium holdings increased to 23.2m lb; NAV per share rose to £6.34; completed £10m buyback.
17706912.take: Market supportive: NAV growth, accretive buyback execution, and strategic uranium accumulation at favourable prices amid strengthening long-term uranium demand fundamentals and constrained supply outlook position company well.

17706910.summary: TotalEnergies has decided to appeal the 25 June 2026 Paris Judicial Court judgment in a duty of vigilance climate case brought by associations. The company argues climate change is a global phenomenon beyond the law's scope, citing the Public Prosecutor's Office position that it is "a matter for everyone" but primarily the international community's responsibility. TotalEnergies contends the duty of vigilance law should not extend to customers' use of products, drawing parallels to the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive which similarly excludes customer activities.
17706910.brief: TotalEnergies appeals Paris court's duty of vigilance climate judgment, argues climate change outside law's scope.
17706910.take: This is a defensive legal move unlikely to move markets materially in near-term; reflects ongoing regulatory/litigation risks for energy majors but appeal outcome remains uncertain and distant.

17707025.summary: Unicorn AIM VCT plc, managed by Unicorn Asset Management Limited, crossed a notification threshold on 23 July 2026 when its voting rights in Huddled Group PLC decreased to 3.59% (29,137,930 shares), down from a previous position of 5.60%. The change was notified to the FCA on 24 July 2026. This represents a material reduction in the shareholder's stake, falling below the 5% disclosure threshold.
17707025.brief: Unicorn Asset Management's holding in Huddled Group falls from 5.60% to 3.59% of voting rights.
17707025.take: A reduction in a major shareholder's stake from 5.6% to 3.6% suggests either a planned diversification or portfolio rebalancing by the VCT; likely a non-event unless broader context signals distress or strategic concerns about Huddled Group.

17707057.summary: AL Sydbank A/S executed 30,000 share buybacks during week 30 (20-24 July 2026) at volume-weighted average prices ranging from DKK 609.17 to DKK 618.64, spending DKK 18.4m. Since the programme's March 2026 launch, the bank has repurchased 947,000 shares for DKK 509.2m of the planned DKK 1.1bn allocation, representing 1.08% of share capital. Execution continues on schedule ahead of the 31 January 2027 completion deadline, conducted via Danske Bank on Copenhagen Stock Exchange (XCSE).
17707057.brief: AL Sydbank repurchased 30,000 shares in week 30 at average price DKK 613.18, progressing its DKK 1.1bn buyback programme.
17707057.take: Routine regulatory disclosure of ongoing capital management; repurchases within expected parameters support share buyback signalling. No material market impact anticipated—standard programme progress.

17707067.summary: Hamak Strategy Limited closed its voluntary warrant exchange offer on 27 July 2026 with 179,906,090 eligible warrants tendered for cancellation, exceeding the 100m minimum threshold by approximately 79.9%. At a one-for-five exchange ratio, the company will issue 35,981,218 new ordinary shares, reducing potential dilution by 143,924,872 shares (80% reduction). No directors participated in the cancellation, signalling confidence in company prospects.
17707067.brief: Hamak Strategy successfully closes warrant exchange offer; 179.9m warrants tendered for cancellation, exceeding 100m minimum by 79.9%.
17707067.take: Positive read: substantial warrant overhang removal simplifies capital structure and reduces future dilution risk, supporting investor clarity on Akoko Gold project and Bitcoin treasury strategy. Board confidence evidenced by director non-participation.

17707065.summary: Metlen Energy & Metals executed share repurchases totalling 128,979 ordinary shares (€1.00 each) via Piraeus Securities on Euronext Athens between 20-24 July 2026, at prices ranging €42.74-€43.92 per share with volume-weighted average of €43.20.
